subject.title: cron: reject webhook URLs with embedded credentials

question: Should cron webhook URLs with userinfo fail closed for existing stored jobs, or should the PR add an upgrade-safe migration/warning path before enforcing rejection?
rationale: The diff is a legitimate security hardening direction, but it changes existing stored cron delivery behavior and the repository policy treats fail-closed config/runtime changes as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Make rejection upgrade-safe before merge
options.body: Add migration or warning behavior plus focused tests for credentialed primary, completion, failure, and legacy webhook targets before enforcing the shared helper rejection.

options.title: Accept deliberate fail-closed behavior
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly decide that existing credential-bearing cron webhook jobs should stop delivering and require operators to move credentials to supported auth mechanisms.

options.title: Pause for cron security policy
options.body: If fail-closed webhook credential handling is not confirmed as the desired cron policy, pause this PR or replace it with a maintainer-owned security design.

recommendation.title: Make rejection upgrade-safe before merge
recommendation.body: Add migration or warning behavior plus focused tests for credentialed primary, completion, failure, and legacy webhook targets before enforcing the shared helper rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: Authored the cron webhook helper and delivery split that this PR changes.
